questions.stem: How are 'in-situ' and 'ex-situ' approaches of biodiversity conservations different from each other ?

Farmers are often suggested to use the following organisms in their crop land so as to improve the soil fertility.
(i) Rhizobium (ii) Anabaena
Explain.
Restriction endonucleases are used in genetic engineering to form recombinant DNA. Explain only with the help of a flow chart the steps carried in the formation of a recombinant DNA.
questions._drawFigure: a flow chart of recombinant DNA formation, three steps joined by downward arrows: (1) the same restriction endonuclease (e.g. EcoRI) cuts both the vector DNA and the foreign DNA at the same palindromic site, a little away from its centre; (2) single-stranded overhangs, 'sticky ends', are left on each fragment; (3) the fragments join at their complementary sticky ends and DNA ligase seals them to form recombinant DNA. The scheme also accepts the NCERT figure 'Action of restriction enzyme' (vector DNA and foreign DNA with GAATTC/CTTAAG sites, EcoRI, sticky ends, recombinant DNA) or the plasmid schematic (foreign DNA and vector DNA (plasmid) cut by the same restriction enzyme, ligases join foreign DNA to plasmid, recombinant DNA molecule).
